title: US 50 ACCIDENT CLAIMS CISNE BOY
full_story:
At about 6:45 last night a two vehicle accident was reported at the intersection of US 50 and Ironwood road.

Clay County Coroner Bryce Henry reports that the accident involved a semi and a side by side.  Henry identified the driver of the side by side as 15-year-old Owen W Bailey of Cisne.  According to Henry, the side by side was traveling west on the shoulder of Route 50 and attempted to make a left turn onto Ironwood Road and for unknown reasons pulled in front of the eastbound semi.  Bailey was taken to the Clay County Hospital where he died of his injuries.

Cisne middle school is reporting that grief counselors will be at the school today for students.

Emergency units from Clay County ambulance and the Xenia Fire Department, Clay County Coroners office, Clay County Sheriff’s Office, Illinois State Police, Flora ESDA and IDOT responded to the accident.  Accident reconstructionist had Highway 50 closed until about 12:15 am.

No other details are available at this time, the accident remains under investigation.

title: FARINA FIRE
full_story:
Two teenaged brothers were killed in a Sunday morning fire in Farina.

Firemen responded to a structure fire at about 9:30 Sunday morning.  Fayette County Coroner David Harris pronounced both 19-year-old Brandon Fulk and 18-year-old Zachary Fulk dead at the scene.  Harris said a younger sibling was able to escape the burning home.  An autopsy on both of those killed will be performed in Springfield today.

Responding firefighters were from Farina, Altamont, Kinmundy-Alma, St. Peter, Edgewood Bi-County, St. Elmo, North Clay and Watson, along with Rural Med EMS, Fayette County Sheriff’s Office, the Farina Police Department, and the Illinois State Fire Marshal’s Office.

title: BURGLARY ARREST
full_story:
On Friday, February 13th the Clay County Sheriff’s Office responded to a report of a burglary in Clay City Township.  It was reported that unknown person entered multiple structures at the property without permission and stole several items.

Sheriff’s deputies were able to identify a suspect during the investigation.  The investigation was forwarded to the Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip Givens for consideration of charges.  Givens obtained an arrest warrant for Steven J. Godfrey, 32, of Flora, for the offenses of Burglary, Theft, and Criminal Damage to Property.

On Wednesday a deputy on routine patrol observed Godfrey on a bicycle traveling on 12th Street in Flora.  The deputy made contact with Godfrey at 9th and Locust Street and took him into custody.  Godfrey was transported to the Clay County Jail.  Godfrey appeared in Clay County Court and was granted Pretrial Release under the “Safe-T Act”.

The charge is merely an accusation and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: FAFSA NIGHT
full_story:
Frontier Community College is hosting a FAFSA Completion Night from 3 to 6 pm tomorrow in the Learning Commons of Cox Hall.

FCC Financial Aid experts will be available to answer questions and assist students and parents in Filing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).  Those attending should bring their FSA ID and 2024 tax returns to simplify the process.

While the event is open to everyone, the FCC Financial Aid staff especially encourages high school seniors who have not yet completed the FAFSA to attend, as it is required by the state for high school graduation.

For more information or if you have questions about the FAFSA, visit www.iecc.edu/financial, or contact FCC Financial Aid at 618-842-3711 extension 4116.

title: CLARK APPOINTED
full_story:
Justice David K. Overstreet and the Illinois Supreme Court announced the appointment of Chelsey Elizabeth Clark as Resident Judge in the Second Judicial Circuit, Richland County.

Ms. Clark is being appointed to fill the vacancy created by the retirement of Judge Ray Vaughn.  The appointment is effective April 17th, and will conclude on December 7th.  She is running unopposed for the seat in the November general election.

“I would like to thank Justice Overstreet and the Illinois Supreme Court for this appointment,” Ms. Clark said.  “It is an honor to serve the citizens of Richland County, and it is a privilege and responsibility I do not take lightly.”

Ms. Clark has served as the Richland County State’s Attorney since 2024.  She previously served as an assistant state’s attorney in Lawrence and Richland counties.  She began her career with Clark Law Office in Olney with a focus on family law, estates, and probate.

Ms. Clark earned her Bachelors degree from Southern Illinois University Carbondale and her Juris Doctor from Southern Illinois University School of Law.

The Second Judicial Circuit includes the counties of Crawford, Edwards, Franklin, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Jefferson, Lawrence, Richland, Wabash, Wayne, and White.

title: CARLYLE LAKE OPENING
full_story:
Spring has arrived, and the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Facilities at Carlyle Lake will soon open for the 2026 recreation season.  This includes the Carlyle Lake Visitor Center, campgrounds, and fish cleaning stations, all of which enrich the visitor experience and offer recreational opportunities on public lands.

Carlyle Lake Visitor Center will be open from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm on Saturdays and Sundays from April 4th through May 24th.  Then will be open Daily from May 25th through September 7th.

Dam West Campground and Dam East-McNair Campground will open on April 3rd.  Boulder Campground open on April 17th and Coles Creek Campground will open May 1st.

Fish cleaning stations will open in mid-April, and beaches will open closer to Memorial Day weekend, depending on weather conditions.

All USACE campgrounds at Carlyle Lake – Dam West, Dam East-McNair, Boulder, and Coles Creek are fully reservable.  Each campsite features a QR Code that visitors can scan onsite to make a reservation, if available.  Reservations can be made up to six months in advance, starting from the current day, through recreation.gov or by calling 877-444-6777.

For more information, contact the Carlyle Lake Project at 618-594-2484.

title: DAY OF GIVING
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges will host its first-ever Day of Giving on Tuesday, March 31st, inviting alumni, businesses and community members to support student success across its four campuses.

The 24-hour event will feature fundraising efforts led by the foundations of Frontier Community College, Lincoln Trail College, Olney Central College and Wabash Valley College. Each campus will focus on raising support for scholarships, programs and initiatives that benefit students.

IECC Vice Chancellor of Institutional Outreach Tona Ambrose said the idea for a coordinated Day of Giving grew out of the district’s recent reorganization and a renewed focus on strengthening alumni engagement.

“IECC has wanted to establish an alumni community for years, and with the collaborative reorganization of our district two years ago, it seemed like the perfect time to create our first Day of Giving,” Ambrose said.  “This event gives each of our college foundations an intentional opportunity to grow partnerships with alumni, businesses and community supporters who care deeply about student success.”

Since its founding in 1971, the Olney Central College Foundation has continually supported student and campus initiatives.

“We are really fortunate to have the Olney Central College Foundation to support all the different activities around campus,” said OCC President Chris Simpson.  “They are great partners, whether we’re looking at things to do in classrooms or working with faculty on providing financial support for innovative practices that they want to bring forward into their classrooms.”

OCC Foundation Executive Director Beth Miller said community support during events like the Day of Giving plays an important role in expanding opportunities for students.

“Community support is vital because Olney Central College serves the people and workforce of the region,” she said.  “When individuals and organizations give back, they are investing in local students and the future of the community.  That partnership helps the college continue expanding opportunities and preparing graduates to contribute to the local economy and community life.”

While scholarships remain a key focus, Miller said the foundation’s work encompasses so much more.

“While scholarships are a major focus, the Foundation also supports a wide range of initiatives that enhance the student experience,” she said.  “This includes funding for classroom equipment, program improvements, and campus projects that benefit students across many areas of study.  The Foundation’s support helps ensure students have the tools and opportunities they need to complete their education and reach their goals.”

Foundation support has helped fund scholarships, new technology, equipment and facility improvements that enhance the student experience.  Recently, the OCC Foundation played an essential role in the construction of the Health Professions Center, pledging more than $150,000 over five years to ensure the inclusion of a modern classroom space within the facility.  Donations toward the project totaled $125,660 last year.

In 2026, the OCC Foundation is supporting a planned $2 million project to renovate four science labs in Dr. Kent L. Wattleworth Hall.  The project will transform third-floor physics, chemistry and two biology labs into modern, high-tech learning spaces, with the foundation assisting through the purchase of state-of-the-art lab equipment.

“That project is getting underway this spring and will continue through the summer,” Simpson said.  “So not only are we going to be renovating those spaces but also upgrading much of the equipment and the materials and supplies the faculty are using and the students have access to.”

Community support remains essential to OCC’s ability to expand opportunities and enhance the educational experience for its students.

“It’s a really difficult time in higher education, particularly in community colleges with funding,” Simpson said.  “There are a number of shortfalls that we’re facing and without having outside support, then I think we would be unable to meet some of the needs of our students and be able to provide them exactly what it is they’re looking for with their post-secondary experience.”

Because of those challenges, Simpson said fundraising efforts such as the Day of Giving, and the Foundation’s annual Campaign for Excellence are essential.

“I hope they recognize that they are directly impacting the educational experience of a student,” Simpson said of donors.  “If you are giving, then know that that money is going to directly impact the students’ experience while they’re attending Olney Central College.”

Simpson also expressed appreciation for the donors and community members who continue to support OCC.

“One of the things that I’ve noticed in the time that I’ve been president is how generous our community is,” he said.  “They support Olney Central College.  We wouldn’t be able to do it without them.”

To participate in OCC’s Day of Giving, visit www.iecc.edu/occ-day-giving.

title: SUMMER JOBS PROGRAM
full_story:
The Illinois Secretary of State’s Office is now accepting applications for its fourth annual summer job program.

Approximately 120 paid positions are available for college, trade school, and graduate students, as well as graduating high school seniors who will be enrolled in college or trade school in the fall.  A limited program is also available for 25 high school students ages 16 and older with all the positions offered across the Secretary of State’s 25 departments and at DMV facilities throughout the state.

Applications are now being accepted at the Secretary of State’s website, at ilsos.gov.summerjobs where applicants must submit a resume, completed application, and a cover letter describing their interest in working at the Secretary of State’s Office, plus applicants can list up to three preferred work locations.
